concept.name: Normal variation day
aliases: normal variation of a normal day
concept.definition: A Market Profile day type between a normal day and a trend day: the initial balance is somewhat narrower than on a normal day, and after the early range forms, longer-timeframe participants drive a one-sided range extension — commonly to roughly twice the initial range — before the market builds value around the extended area.
concept.intuition: The day starts quietly like a normal day, but partway through, bigger players step in on one side and push the auction to new ground.
concept.mechanics: Identified by an average initial balance followed by a decisive one-sided range extension (often emerging mid-session), with trade then concentrating around the point of control of the enlarged distribution.
concept.failure_modes: The boundary with normal and trend days is judgmental — the size and timing of the extension that qualifies a day as a 'normal variation' is a convention, and misclassification shifts the tactical read.
concept.misconceptions: The day type is a post-hoc structural classification, not an intraday prediction; expecting a normal-variation day because the morning 'looks like one' has no statistical guarantee.
concept.example: After a 25-point initial balance, G-period extends the range another 25 points to the upside and the afternoon accepts the higher prices — a normal variation up day.
